title: Adding a string id alongside the numeric one (sound control)

source.note: Written by the repository author (v0.2 case set).

input.objective: Stop order IDs from being corrupted in JavaScript clients now that IDs are 64-bit Snowflake integers above 2^53.
constraints: Fix must be live within two weeks.
No change to how IDs are generated.
input.context: GET /v1/orders/{id} and list endpoints return `"id": 1234567890123456789` as a JSON number. The web frontend already displays wrong IDs for new orders. Consumers: the web app (deployed with the API), iOS app (Swift Codable `let id: Int64`), Android app (Kotlin + Moshi `val id: Long`), ~40 partner integrations using SDKs generated from our OpenAPI spec (`type: integer, format: int64`). Path parameters are parsed server-side as strings.
input.proposed_solution: Keep `id` exactly as it is and add a new field `id_str` (string) to every object that carries an order ID, including nested references (`order_id` gets `order_id_str`). Update the OpenAPI spec additively and regenerate SDKs; switch the web app to `id_str` in the same release. Accept both numeric and string forms in path and query parameters. Announce `id` as deprecated for JavaScript consumers in the changelog and docs, measure `id_str` adoption from partner SDK user agents, and only consider removing the numeric field in a future v2.
input.environment: Mobile apps are released weekly via the stores; users update at their own pace.

ground_truth.material_issue: None: the proposal is a sound decision for the stated context.
ground_truth.notes: Sound control (same problem as api-id-type-change, good proposal).
